explanation_steps: **Sclerenchyma** is the primary supporting tissue in plants. It is composed of dead cells with very thick, lignified secondary walls. questions.stem: Which of the following is classified as a monosaccharide?
explanation_steps: Monosaccharides are the simplest form of carbohydrates (simple sugars). Glucose, fructose, and galactose are common examples. Sucrose and lactose are disaccharides, while glycogen and starch are polysaccharides.

explanation_steps: Insulin lowers blood sugar by signaling the liver and muscle cells to take up glucose and store it as **glycogen** (a process called glycogenesis).

explanation_steps: The plasma membrane (cell membrane) is described by the 'Fluid Mosaic Model,' consisting primarily of a phospholipid bilayer (lipids) with embedded proteins.

explanation_steps: Scurvy is a disease resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid). It leads to symptoms like bleeding gums, weakness, and skin spots.

explanation_steps: Textbook (G10 p.8): 'A severe protein inadequacy in the diet results in kwashiorkor', common in children after weaning.

options.D: protons is greater than the number of neutrons.
options.E: protons is always less than the number of neutrons.

explanation_steps: An atom is electrically neutral because it has as many electrons (−) as protons (+) (G9 p.50).
The number of neutrons can be less, equal or greater (e.g. H-1 has none). Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: An element "$$ X $$ " has two isotopes, which may be represented as $$ ^{238}X $$ and $$ ^{235}X $$. How does $$ ^{238}X $$ differ from $$ ^{235}X $$?

options.A: It has 3 more protons and 3 more electrons.
options.B: It has 3 more protons but same number of electrons.
options.C: It has 3 more neutrons and 3 more electrons.
options.D: It has 3 more neutrons but same number of protons.
options.E: Both have the same atomic mass.

explanation_steps:
**Isotopes** are atoms of the same element that have the **same number of protons** (same atomic number) but a **different number of neutrons** (different mass number). 
Difference = $$ 238 - 235 = 3 $$. Thus, $$ ^{238}X $$ has **3 more neutrons**.

explanation_steps: Intramolecular forces are the chemical bonds that hold atoms together: ionic, covalent and metallic bonds. Intermolecular forces act between molecules: hydrogen bonds, dipole–dipole, ion–dipole and dispersion (van der Waals) forces (G10 pp.41–42, 58–61).

explanation_steps: Proteins are organic compounds made up of amino acids. All proteins contain Carbon (C), Hydrogen (H), Oxygen (O), and Nitrogen (N). Sodium (Na) is an electrolyte/ion found in body fluids but is not a structural part of the protein molecule itself.

similar_questions.stem: One of the following **is not** a constituent of a nucleic acid molecule.
explanation_steps: Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are composed of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and phosphorous (found in the phosphate group). Sulphur is a characteristic component of many proteins but is absent in nucleic acids.

explanation_steps: Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon compounds (G12 p.24); all organic compounds contain carbon (usually with hydrogen).

questions.stem: Pollination can be described best as the

options.A: fusing of the egg nucleus with the pollen nucleus.
options.B: transfer of a pollen grain to the pistil of a flower.
options.C: formation of male and female sex cells.

explanation_steps: The ovaries are the female gonads: they produce eggs (ova) and the hormones oestrogen and progesterone (G11 p.27).
The Fallopian tube carries the egg (and is the site of fertilisation); the uterus holds the developing fetus. Answer: C.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Molality ($$ m $$) = $$ \frac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{kg of solvent}} $$.

similar_questions.stem: A uniform meter stick is pivoted at its center. It carries a block of mass 500 g at one of its ends (Point A) and another block of mass 400 g is placed at the other end (Point B). A mass of 250 g balances the meter stick placed at a distance of
explanation_steps: The stick's own weight acts at the pivot (centre), so it gives no moment. Each end is 50 cm from the pivot.

Moments (in g·cm, g cancels): A side 500 × 50 = 25 000; B side 400 × 50 = 20 000. The extra 5000 on A's side must be balanced by the 250 g mass on B's side: 250 × d = 5000 → d = 20 cm from the pivot (G10 pp.30–31).

$$ 720 = \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 $$
$$ 720 = 5t^2 $$
$$ t^2 = 144 \implies t = 12 \text{ s} $$

**Step 2: Find the horizontal distance ($$ x $$).**

questions.stem: The wavelength of a radio wave is $$ 300 \text{ m} $$ broadcasted through a frequency of $$ 6 \text{ MHz} $$. The speed of the radio wave in m/s is
explanation_steps:

$$ v = 1800 \times 10^6 \text{ m/s} = 1.8 \times 10^9 \text{ m/s} $$.

How many moles of oxygen are present in 49g $$ H_2SO_4 $$?
**molar mass: H = 1g; O = 16g; S = 32g**
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate the molar mass of $$ H_2SO_4 $$.**
$$ M = (2 \times 1) + 32 + (4 \times 16) = 2 + 32 + 64 = 98 \text{ g/mol} $$

**Step 2: Calculate the number of moles of $$ H_2SO_4 $$ in 49g.**
$$ n = \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{molar mass}} = \frac{49 \text{ g}}{98 \text{ g/mol}} = 0.5 \text{ mol} $$

**Step 3: Calculate the moles of Oxygen (O) atoms.**
One molecule of $$ H_2SO_4 $$ contains 4 atoms of Oxygen. Therefore, 1 mole of $$ H_2SO_4 $$ contains 4 moles of Oxygen atoms.
$$ \text{Moles of O} = 0.5 \text{ mol } H_2SO_4 \times 4 = 2 \text{ mol} $$

**Result:** 2 mol (Option C).
